name: Prompt Chaining (visual/workflow composition)
executive_summary: Compose multi-step LLM prompt sequences as an explicit visual/workflow graph, treating chain design itself as a first-class engineering problem.
description: Rather than a single reasoning technique, this is a design methodology and tooling approach for building, debugging, and iterating on multi-prompt chains — predating most later 'agent framework' tooling. Useful less for the specific prompts it proposes and more for the design principles (visibility into intermediate outputs, easy re-ordering of steps) it established.
when_to_use: Designing or debugging any multi-step prompt pipeline, regardless of the specific reasoning technique used within it.
when_not_to_use: Single-call prompting with no chain structure to design.
known_pitfalls: A workflow/tooling paper, not a reasoning-quality technique — doesn't itself improve accuracy, only development ergonomics.

primary_source.title: PromptChainer: Chaining Large Language Model Prompts through Visual Programming

usage_templates.template: For each node in the chain, specify: (1) input variables consumed from prior nodes, (2) the prompt template, (3) output variables produced, (4) whether output feeds one downstream node or several. Node: {{node_name}}. Inputs: {{input_vars}}. Template: {{node_template}}. Outputs: {{output_vars}}.

variables.name: input_vars
variables.description: Variables this node consumes from earlier nodes

variables.name: output_vars
variables.description: Variables this node produces for later nodes

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
